data.title: IGL, Northern Railway join hands to replace LPG, diesel with PNG at 22 locations
data.description:
Indraprastha Gas Ltd (IGL) has signed an agreement with the Delhi Division of Northern Railway to supply piped natural gas (PNG) to 22 railway establishments across Delhi-NCR, as the city gas distributor steps up efforts to replace conventional fuels with natural gas under the government's PNG Drive 3.0.

The agreement will initially facilitate the supply of around 3,000 standard cubic metres of gas per day (SCMD), replacing consumption of approximately 500 kg of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and 2,500 litres of diesel daily, IGL said in a statement.

The proposed conversion will cover railway mechanised laundries, officers' rest houses, base kitchens, running rooms, subordinate rest houses and guard and ticket examiner lobbies across Delhi, Ghaziabad and Gautam Buddha Nagar.

The mechanised laundries at Delhi Sarai Rohilla, Old Delhi, Anand Vihar Terminal, Hazrat Nizamuddin and New Delhi will use PNG for boiler operations.

IGL expects consumption under the initiative to increase to 8,000-10,000 SCMD in the coming years as pipeline infrastructure and connectivity expand across its authorised geographical areas, including Ajmer, Banda, Rewari and Muzaffarnagar.

The agreement, signed on Friday in the presence of senior officials from both organisations, is part of a broader push to expand natural gas consumption among institutional and commercial users and reduce reliance on imported fuels.

"This partnership brings together two major organisations committed to nation building. Indian Railways has chosen IGL as its collaborative partner to replace LPG with PNG and this MoU will facilitate the substitution of a substantial quantity of LPG with natural gas, thereby helping reduce import dependence and the associated subsidy burden," IGL Chairman Subhankar Sen said.

He added that the collaboration could pave the way for a wider transition from LPG to PNG across the Indian Railways network, extending its impact beyond Delhi.

Delhi Division Railway Manager Pushpesh Raman Tripathi said the agreement would help reduce energy costs for the national transporter and that PNG connectivity could subsequently be extended to railway hospitals and residential colonies.

"This MoU will help reduce substantial energy costs for Indian Railways and we plan to extend PNG connectivity to railway hospitals and residential colonies in the future as well," he said.

The partnership comes as IGL intensifies efforts to expand household PNG connections under the government's National PNG Drive 3.0.

On October 28, the company launched promotional incentives offering a Rs 2,000 discount on standard domestic PNG registration charges and Rs 500 worth of free gas after activation of a connection. The initiative seeks to accelerate registrations and gas-in conversions across Delhi-NCR and other authorised areas through outreach programmes and partnerships with resident welfare associations and apartment owners' bodies.

IGL Managing Director Kumar Shanker said the initiative was aimed at extending pipeline-based natural gas to a wider range of institutional consumers, while structured outreach and partnerships with residential associations would help speed up household connectivity.

The twin initiatives reflect the government's broader effort to expand natural gas use in transport, industry, commercial establishments and households. Replacing LPG and diesel with pipeline gas can reduce the need for cylinder handling and fuel storage while providing a continuous supply, although the actual cost and emissions benefits would depend on procurement prices, end-use efficiency and the fuels displaced.

IGL operates city gas distribution networks across 34 districts in 11 geographical areas spanning Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan.

Its infrastructure includes more than 30,000 km of pipelines and over 1,000 CNG stations, serving more than 2.5 million CNG vehicles and nearly 3.5 million PNG-connected households.

The railway agreement offers a potential institutional template for expanding PNG adoption across public-sector establishments, while the household incentives seek to build demand at the consumer level. A wider rollout across railway facilities could provide a sizable additional market for city gas distributors and help advance India's efforts to diversify its fuel mix and reduce dependence on imported energy. data.title: Escorts Kubota To Hike Tractor Prices Across Three Brands From November
data.description:
Price revision across Kubota, Farmtrac and Powertrac ranges will vary by model, variant and geography

Escorts Kubota Limited (EKL) will increase prices across its Kubota, Farmtrac and Powertrac tractor ranges from November 2026, following the festive season. The company said the revision was driven by rising input costs, including raw materials, energy, logistics and manufacturing expenses.

The price increase will vary across models, variants and geographies within the three tractor portfolios. Revised prices will be available through authorised dealerships.

The company attributed the increase in costs to inflationary trends and ongoing geopolitical uncertainties. It said it had undertaken cost optimisation and operational efficiency initiatives over the past several months to limit the impact on customers. EKL also absorbed a substantial portion of the increased costs.

However, with input costs continuing to remain elevated, the company said the price revision had become necessary to partially offset higher manufacturing and operating expenses.

Escorts Kubota Expands Tractor Portfolio

Alongside the price revision, EKL has continued to expand its tractor offerings across its three brands.

Recent additions include the Farmtrac PROMAXX series, Powertrac Shaurya series and an expanded Digitrac range. The company has also expanded its Kubota portfolio with the NeoStar and MU series.

These product additions, supported by dealer network expansion, are aimed at providing farmers with a wider choice of tractors suited to different agricultural requirements.

Escorts Kubota operates in the agricultural and construction equipment segments. Its product portfolio includes tractors under the Kubota, Farmtrac and Powertrac brands, along with specialised agricultural machinery and construction equipment.

The company has a dealer network serving customers across India and international markets.

data.title: Reliance Jewels Onboards Gopa Kumar To Lead Business
data.description:
The retail veteran joins Reliance Jewels after a seven-year stint as COO of Bhima Jewels, bringing over two decades of experience

Reliance Jewels, part of Reliance Retail, has appointed Gopa Kumar as Head of Reliance Jewels, bringing an experienced retail executive on board to lead the jewellery business. Kumar announced his new role through a LinkedIn post, stating that he was looking forward to building on the brand's legacy and identifying fresh opportunities for growth.

He joins Reliance Jewels after a seven-year stint as Chief Operating Officer at Bhima Jewels, where he had been associated with the retailer since 2019. During his tenure, he oversaw operations at the jewellery business before announcing his departure and return to Mumbai.

Kumar brings more than two decades of experience across organised retail and consumer-facing businesses. His professional background includes leadership positions at Future Group, Shoppers Stop, Hindustan Unilever, Next Retail and Future Retail, among others.

His experience spans business strategy, profit and loss management, retail operations, category management, marketing, digital initiatives and business expansion. He has also worked across different retail formats, including department stores, convenience retail, e-commerce, luxury, lifestyle and speciality retail.

At Reliance Jewels, Kumar is expected to focus on business strategy, retail expansion, brand development and customer experience, alongside driving revenue growth and operational performance. His responsibilities will also include strengthening merchandising and product strategy, digital and omnichannel initiatives, and organisational capabilities.

The appointment comes as Reliance Jewels continues to operate within India's organised jewellery retail market, with a portfolio spanning gold, diamond and silver jewellery and a nationwide network of company-owned showrooms.

data.title: Advance Gold Helps Optimise Our Working Capital: Sky Gold and Diamonds CFO
data.description:
Siddharth Sipani outlines how the model is reducing inventory funding requirements and supporting higher manufacturing volumes

For Sky Gold and Diamonds, managing working capital has become an important part of its growth strategy as it seeks to balance higher production volumes with cash flow discipline. The company reported positive operating cash flow of approximately Rs 30 crore in Q1 FY27, alongside 78 per cent revenue growth, following a year of negative operating cash flow.

Siddharth Sipani, CFO of Sky Gold and Diamonds, discusses the operational changes behind this shift, the role of the Advance Gold model, export opportunities and the financial priorities of a growing B2B jewellery manufacturer.

You have spoken about deliberately holding back from pushing sales growth even higher to protect that cash flow. What did it take internally to make that trade-off between growth and cash discipline?

Q1 FY27 marked an important step in our financial progression, with strong revenue growth accompanied by positive operating cash flow. Our focus has been on sustaining that balance across sales growth, profitability and working capital.

We have focused on receivables, inventory and business mix, while deploying part of the cash generated by gold jewellery into higher-margin studded products. Approximately Rs 30 crore of positive operating cash flow was achieved in the June 2026 quarter alongside 78 per cent revenue growth, reflecting the progress of this approach.

Sky Gold raised Rs 270 crore through a Qualified Institutional Placement. How are you thinking about deploying that capital alongside the company's shift towards its 'Advance Gold' model aimed at reducing inventory risk?

The QIP supported an earlier phase of expansion. Raised in October 2024, the proceeds were almost fully utilised by December that year towards the working capital requirements of the Group. Due to this fundraising, the company has been able to scale its operations from 250 kg to 750 kg. The Advance Gold model of the business helps in optimising the company's working capital needs, and funds released from this business model are deployed towards serving other customers. This helps in better overall capacity utilisation and achieving higher volumes and PAT for the Group.

Sky Gold has been moving towards reducing inventory risk and improving capital efficiency through this Advance Gold approach. What has been the biggest operational change internally to make that shift work while the business keeps growing this fast?

As Advance Gold becomes a larger part of our business, operational visibility is increasingly important to capital efficiency. Our technology and enterprise resource planning (ERP) initiatives support better tracking of data and the movement of goods across the organisation.

Alongside this, our existing facilities offer headroom for growth. Higher utilisation improves cost absorption and allows us to generate more output from infrastructure already in place. At the same time, we have existing manufacturing capacity that can support further growth. As we improve utilisation, we can scale the business more efficiently.

Exports to the Middle East and Southeast Asia have been a growing part of Sky Gold's business alongside deepening retail partnerships in India. How do you see that export mix evolving as the company scales further?

Exports are an important part of our growth strategy, both for market diversification and their attractive financial profile. We are targeting an export contribution of around 20 per cent by FY30, supported by our Dubai base and established presence in the UAE, Bahrain, Singapore and Malaysia.

We are also developing opportunities in the UK and Japan. Our participation in the London jewellery exhibition generated initial order interest of Rs 30-45 crore from buyers across these markets. Strengthening our overseas teams and channels gives us a broader platform to build this business.

Before joining Sky Gold, you spent over eight years as Group CFO at Gold Star Jewellery and earlier led M&A financial due diligence at EY. What from leading due diligence on other companies' deals has shaped how you run finance at a fast-scaling listed company now?

My experience across audit, M&A consulting and the jewellery industry has given me exposure to businesses at different stages and across different functions.

At Sky Gold, that experience helps me look at growth from both a financial and operational perspective. We are focused on improving profitability, cash flow and working capital as the business expands.

Technology is another important part of this journey. With better ERP systems and data visibility, we can make decisions faster and manage a growing business more effectively.

Sky Gold operates as a B2B gold jewellery manufacturer supplying organised retailers rather than selling directly to consumers. What is distinct about managing the finance function for a B2B manufacturing model in an industry that is traditionally thought of as consumer-facing?

The B2B model means our financial focus is very closely linked to manufacturing and working capital. We look at areas such as receivables, inventory, profitability and capacity utilisation on a continuous basis.

Advance Gold is particularly useful in this model because customers provide the gold, allowing us to focus on the manufacturing side without the same working capital requirement.

Exports also add to the efficiency of the model, with higher return on capital employed (ROCE) and lower receivable days. Overall, our focus is on building a sustainable business that can grow at scale while becoming more efficient and generating stronger returns.

data.title: Shraddha Bhatt Dave Takes Over As EMA India Chief Financial Officer
data.description:
The appointment takes effect from 30 October following the company's takeover by new management and the resignation of its previous CFO

EMA India has appointed Shraddha Bhatt Dave as its Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and Key Managerial Personnel (KMP), effective 30 October 2026. The appointment follows the recent takeover of the company by new management and the resignation of the previous CFO.

The Board of Directors approved the appointment at a meeting held on Friday, 30 October 2026, based on recommendations from the Audit Committee and the Nomination and Remuneration Committee. The board noted that the company had been identifying a suitable candidate to fill the vacancy created by the former CFO's departure.

Shraddha Bhatt Dave is a Chartered Accountant with over 15 years of experience in financial governance, accounting, audit assurance and regulatory compliance within multinational environments.

Her professional experience includes managing statutory audits, Goods and Services Tax (GST) and tax compliance, as well as cross-border financial reporting under Indian and US Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) standards.

She has also worked on strengthening internal control frameworks, identifying financial irregularities and improving transparency in finance operations.

In the same board meeting, the directors accepted the resignation of Awashesh Dixit as Secretarial Auditor. Dixit, a Practising Company Secretary holding Membership No. F10860 and Certificate of Practice (COP) No. 15398, cited his inability to continue in the role. His cessation was effective 30 October 2026.

Regulatory Disclosure Details

The company disclosed the appointments and resignation under Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.

data.title: Shyam Metalics Q2 results: Company records 88% YoY jump in net profit; margins improve
data.description:
Shyam Metalics has announced its results for Q2 of FY27 on Saturday, October 31. The Kolkata-based company reported strong numbers, with profit and margin figures improving on a year-on-year basis.

Shyam Metallics Q2 Results

The company reported a major 88.5% YoY jump in its net profit, with the profit figure for the September-bound quarter coming in at ₹493.4 crore, as against ₹261.8 crore in Q2 of FY26. When it comes to the top-line numbers, the metal company recorded revenue of ₹5,960 crore in the quarter gone by, which was higher than the previous year's ₹4,467 crore. This marked a year-on-year rise of 33.4% in revenue numbers.

Now, when we look at the profitability of the company over the previous quarter, the company's Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortisation, or EBITDA, surged by 52.6%, with EBITDA for the quarter rising to ₹823 crore, compared to ₹539 Cr in 2025. Finally, the company also improved margin to 13.8%, with a 170-basis-point rise from the previous cycle's 12.1%.

Q1 Recap Of Shyam Metallics

Sequentially speaking, in Q1FY27, the company's net profit rose by 18% year-on-year, reaching ₹345 crore compared to ₹282 crore previously. For the quarter, revenue increased by 23% from the previous year, amounting to ₹5,455 crore, up from ₹4,423 crore.

Earnings Before Interest, Tax, Depreciation and Amortisation (EBITDA) for the quarter was ₹765 crore, reflecting a 32% increase from the ₹580 crore reported in the same quarter last year. Additionally, the EBITDA margin for this period improved by 90 basis points from the previous year, rising to 14% from 13.1%.

Stock Performance

A quick look at the stock performance leads us to a stock that has had a strong showing in the recent past; in the latest session, on Friday, the company's shares rose by over 2%.

In the past month, the share price has increased in value by 10%, and 10 months into 2026, Shyam Metallics' shares have surged by over 37% this year. The current stock price sits at ₹1163 per piece, away from the 52-week high of ₹1,240.50 per piece.

data.title: Ratnaveer Precision Engineering reports 35.5 percent revenue, 38.9 percent EBITDA and 56.1 percent PAT growth in Q2 FY27; new CCL Plant 75 percent complete
data.description:
Mumbai, Oct. 31 -- Ratnaveer Precision Engineering Limited has announced its unaudited financial results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026, reporting strong year-on-year growth across key financial parameters.

Alongside its financial performance, the company continues to advance its capacity expansion plans, with its new CCL plant progressing towards completion and currently approximately 75% complete. The company reports strong financial performance for Q2 and H1 FY27, while advancing its new CCL plant towards completion, with machinery delivery expected by mid-November 2026 and trial runs targeted to commence by December 20, 2026.

Financial Performance Highlights

During Q2 FY27, the company recorded strong growth across its key financial indicators compared with the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.

- Revenue from Operations: Rs.387.24 crore, registering growth of 35.5% YoY, compared with Rs.285.87 crore.

- EBITDA: Rs.42.16 crore, registering growth of 38.9% YoY, compared with Rs.30.35 crore.

- EBITDA Margin: 10.89%, compared with 10.62% in the corresponding period last year.

- Profit After Tax (PAT): Rs.24.10 crore, registering growth of 56.1% YoY, compared with Rs.15.43 crore.

- PAT Margin: 6.22%, compared with 5.40% in the corresponding period last year.

For H1 FY27, the company reported:

- Revenue from Operations: Rs.701.87 crore, registering growth of 27.5% YoY, compared with Rs.550.49 crore.

- EBITDA: Rs.78.14 crore, registering growth of 35.5% YoY, compared with Rs.57.15 crore.

- EBITDA Margin: 11.13%, compared with 10.38% in the corresponding period last year.

- Profit After Tax (PAT): Rs.42.33 crore, registering growth of 39.4% YoY, compared with Rs.30.38 crore.

- PAT Margin: 6.03%, compared with 5.52% in the corresponding period last year.

The financial performance reflects growth in revenue alongside an improvement in profitability and operating margins during the reporting periods. Ratnaveer Precision Engineering Limited remains focused on strengthening its operating performance while progressing with planned investments in manufacturing infrastructure and capacity development.

New CCL Plant Reaches 75% Completion

The company's new CCL plant has achieved approximately 75% completion, with machinery installation and the establishment of supporting utilities representing the key remaining activities before trial operations can begin.

Machinery delivery is expected by mid-November 2026. The schedule has experienced a slight delay due to port connectivity constraints and a shortage of shipping containers amid ongoing global uncertainty.

Following the arrival of the machinery, the company plans to complete installation and establish the required utilities. Trial runs are expected to commence by December 20, 2026, with an anticipated trial period of approximately one month.

The upcoming phase will focus on assessing equipment performance and operational readiness. Completion of these activities will represent a key step towards progressing the facility from the development stage to trial operations.

Focus on Capacity Expansion

The new CCL plant forms part of the company's efforts to expand its manufacturing infrastructure and strengthen its production capabilities. With the project progressing towards completion, the immediate focus remains on machinery installation, utility readiness and the commencement of trial runs.

The development represents an important operational milestone for Ratnaveer Precision Engineering, with the next phase centred on completing the remaining work and evaluating the facility through trial operations. The company continues to pursue its expansion plans alongside its ongoing business activities.

data.title: Three stocks with strong order books to watch amid India's data-centre boom
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- With India's data-centre capacity set for a sharp expansion, investors are looking beyond quarterly earnings to identify the companies positioned to benefit from the infrastructure spending. Their order books offer a window into that opportunity, providing a measure of future revenue visibility as the artificial intelligence (AI) build-out gathers pace.

One of the defining themes of the Q2 FY27 earnings season is the capital expenditure cycle linked to India's data-centre and AI infrastructure build-out. The country's live data-centre capacity has crossed roughly 1.8 GW, following a record addition of 258 MW in the first half of FY27, and is projected to reach about 10.5 GW by 2031.

For investors, the scale of this expansion makes order books an important metric alongside revenue and profit growth. They indicate the volume of business companies have secured and offer clues to the potential trajectory of future revenues.

Three companies stand out for their exposure to different parts of this infrastructure chain: building facilities, powering projects and providing the optical connectivity that data centres need.

Larsen & Toubro

Larsen & Toubro (L&T), India's largest engineering and construction conglomerate, was incorporated in 1938. It operates across projects, hi-tech manufacturing and services, with businesses spanning infrastructure and utilities, energy, manufacturing and products, and technology platforms and services. The last houses its expanding data-centre, semiconductor and digital-platform businesses.

International orders account for 54% of its order backlog.

L&T reported record second quarter results, with revenue rising 16% year-on-year to Rs.78,700 crore and profit after tax increasing 33% to Rs.5,200 crore. Order inflows surged 28% to a quarterly record of Rs.1,47,700 crore. Its consolidated order book stood at Rs.8,53,500 crore as of 30 September, up 28%.

Management attributed the performance to a "resilient portfolio and disciplined growth", with record order inflows led by Ultra Mega and Mega orders in the energy segment.

The company has identified an addressable pipeline of about Rs.10 lakh crore in the near term. Data centres, semiconductors and green hydrogen are among the businesses it is positioning as future growth drivers, supported by cash conversion and a prudent balance sheet.

Power Mech Projects

Power Mech Projects operates across four business segments: Industrial Construction, covering engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) and the erection of boiler-turbine-generator systems; Industrial Services, including operations and maintenance; Infrastructure Construction; and Mining Development and Operations (MDO).

Its client base includes NTPC, BHEL, the Adani Group, JSW and Vedanta.

Revenue has grown at an annual rate of more than 17% to Rs.6,060 crore in FY26. The momentum continued into Q1 FY27, when revenue rose 26% to Rs.1,624 crore.

The company's order backlog, including MDO, stood at Rs.56,650 crore as of 30 September 2026. It reported order inflows of Rs.3,113 crore so far in FY27 and has set a target of Rs.12,000 crore for the full year.

Management expects margins to recover as its MDO business scales up. The company is also shifting towards integrated balance-of-plant (BOP) EPC delivery and higher-margin operations and maintenance work. Multi-decade mining contracts provide a base of recurring, long-term revenue.

Sterlite Technologies

Sterlite Technologies (STL) operates across the optical connectivity value chain, from optical fibre and fibre cables to specialty cables and connectivity solutions. It serves data centres and cloud companies, telecommunications operators, citizen networks and large enterprises across more than 100 countries.

The company describes itself as India's largest end-to-end optical manufacturer and holds roughly 9% of the global optical fibre cable market outside China. Its data-centre business is anchored by its Neural portfolio, designed for the AI era.

STL's order book stood at Rs.35,274 crore as of 30 September 2026, up 4.6 times since the beginning of the year, supported by multi-year agreements with hyperscalers.

The company is targeting revenue of Rs.20,000 crore by FY29 and has raised its EBITDA margin ambition to more than 30%. Data centres already accounted for 33% of its revenue in the first half of FY27.

What investors should watch

The AI and data-centre investment cycle offers opportunities across construction, power and connectivity. But its sustainability depends in part on hyperscalers continuing to commit substantial capital to infrastructure. Spending could moderate if funding costs rise.

A large order book can improve revenue visibility, but it does not guarantee execution, profitability or stock-market returns. Investors also need to assess order quality, execution timelines, margins, corporate governance and valuations before making investment decisions. Each company's fundamentals and risks warrant independent scrutiny.

Happy investing.

data.title: Google Just Got AI To Talk From Space — Project Suncatcher Scores First In-Orbit TPU Response After SpaceX Launch
data.description:
Key points:
  • Google said it reached its “Hello World” milestone this week when it successfully received the first AI response from a data center-class TPU operating in orbit.
  • During a ground-station pass, the team sent a prompt to an onboard Gemma 4 open model, asking it to generate a haiku about being in space.
  • As the satellite passed over Svalbard, Norway, Google received the response back on Earth.

Alphabet Inc.’s (GOOG, GOOGL) Google has gotten artificial intelligence to talk from space for the first time, marking an early milestone in its ambitious Project Suncatcher effort to explore whether AI computing could eventually move beyond Earth.

The breakthrough came weeks after Google's prototype satellite launched into orbit aboard a Space Exploration Technologies Corp.’s (SPCX) rideshare mission. The satellite has now completed its initial commissioning work, including powering up its onboard TPU trays and running early machine learning workloads.

Alphabet’s Class A shares closed 1% lower in Friday’s regular trading session, while SpaceX shares fell more than 6%.

Project Suncatcher Gets Its First AI Response

Google on Friday said it reached its “Hello World” milestone this week when it successfully received the first AI response from a data center-class TPU operating in orbit.

During a ground-station pass, the team sent a prompt to an onboard Gemma 4 open model, asking it to generate a haiku about being in space. As the satellite passed over Svalbard, Norway, Google received the response back on Earth: “Blue marble below. Data streams in silent grace. Starlight feeds my core.”

The team then moved beyond the initial demonstration, testing space-themed limericks and prompts designed to report telemetry and the technical status of the payload systems.

This comes amid Google’s efforts to use the prototype to determine whether its TPU hardware can reliably perform machine learning workloads while exposed to the harsh conditions of space.

What’s Next For Google's AI Chips In Space

The next phase will focus on how the TPUs perform under thermal stress and radiation exposure in orbit, which are two key challenges for any future attempt to deploy computing infrastructure in space.

Google's longer-term vision is to investigate whether solar power and the physical environment of space could eventually support scalable machine learning infrastructure. But the company is still at an early research stage, with the current satellite primarily serving as a test bed for hardware performance and reliability.

The results from the prototype will help determine whether Google can progress to its next planned milestone: two interconnected satellites in 2027.

For now, the successful AI response provides an important proof point that data center-class TPU hardware can execute a machine learning workload in orbit and communicate the result back to Earth.

Musk, Bezos See Bigger Potential for Data Centers in Space

Google's experiment comes as the idea of moving AI infrastructure into orbit gains attention from some of tech's biggest names. Earlier in May this year, Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) and Blue Origin founder Jeff Bezos called SpaceX CEO Elon Musk's proposal for space-based data centers a “very realistic” idea, although he said Musk's timeline could be overly ambitious.

Bezos said the economics ultimately depend on two major factors, which are rising energy costs for terrestrial data centers and a dramatic decline in launch costs. He estimated launch costs would need to fall by roughly 10 times for the concept to become viable at scale.

What Retail Investors Think Of GOOGL Stock

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Alphabet trended in the ‘extremely bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

GOOGL stock is down 11% year-to-date, while SPCX stock is down 10%. The Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) is up 12% over the past 12 months, while the iShares U.S. Technology ETF (IYW) is up 22%.

data.title: India must boost domestic energy exploration, renewables to cut import dependence: PHDCCI President
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- India needs to accelerate domestic oil and gas exploration, expand renewable energy generation and promote electric mobility to reduce its dependence on energy imports and strengthen economic resilience amid global uncertainties, Anil Gupta, President of PHDCCI and Chairman and Managing Director of KEI Industries Limited, said.

Talking to the media, Gupta called for greater private sector participation in domestic oil and gas exploration, supported by favourable contractual terms.

"We should try to do more and more exploration, especially by roping in the private sector and giving them very good contractual terms so that they push for more and more oil and gas exploration," he said.

He also called for greater utilisation of India's available energy resources, including solar, wind and coal, alongside wider adoption of electric passenger and commercial vehicles to reduce dependence on imported oil.

Gupta said India had managed the impact of the global oil price surge relatively well, with retail petrol and diesel prices rising by around 10-15 per cent, compared with increases of more than 100 per cent in some other countries.

On India's economic resilience, he attributed the country's growth momentum to domestic consumption, the China-plus-one strategy and expanding access to international markets through free trade agreements (FTAs).

"One of the reasons that India remains immune to the world crisis is that our own good consuming population," Gupta said, adding that the China-plus-one strategy had also supported industrial growth and exports.

He said the FTAs signed with Europe, the UAE and other countries would gradually support exports, although developing markets and building trust between buyers and sellers would take time. He expected these agreements to begin delivering results over the next two to three years.

On critical minerals, Gupta said India was almost entirely dependent on imports for copper, with around 95 per cent of its requirements sourced from overseas, while the country was self-reliant in aluminium. He expressed optimism that government initiatives to promote rare earth mineral exploration and production would help India move towards self-reliance over the next two to three years.

Ranjeet Mehta, CEO and Secretary General of PHDCCI, highlighted the need to improve awareness among micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) about government support schemes and international trade opportunities.

"Most of the MSMEs in our country are totally unaware of these schemes," Mehta said, adding that PHDCCI was conducting outreach programmes at district and smaller-city levels to familiarise businesses with platforms such as GeM and TReDS.

Gupta said India could achieve GDP growth of more than 7 per cent in FY27, adding that the country's economic outlook remained positive.

data.title: IMD weather alert: Heavy rain for Karnataka, Andhra, Kerala; no showers in Delhi- What you need to know before going out
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast rain, thunderstorms, and gusty winds across several states on Saturday, October 31, amid a warning that a new weather system is brewing in the Bay of Bengal, even as the remnants of Cyclone Arnab continue to impact inland areas.

Areas including Arunachal Pradesh, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, and Kerala may experience heavy rainfall, while thunderstorms accompanied by strong winds are expected in states such as Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karnataka, and Telangana.

Delhi, meanwhile, is expected to see partly cloudy skies, with no rainfall.

No rainfall is expected in Delhi today, October 31, a day after the city recorded its lowest October day temperature in 75 years, with the maximum plunging to 20.7 degrees Celsius amid two days of persistent rain.

Delhi is, however, expected to experience a partly cloudy sky with winds blowing from the northwest and southeast at 5-10 kmph.

"The maximum and minimum temperatures over Delhi are likely to be in the range of 26 degC to 28 degC and 15 degC to 17 degC respectively," IMD noted

On Friday, Delhi also recorded its wettest October day in four years and the sixth-wettest since 1951. The city also logged its cleanest October air on Friday, with the AQI settling at 60, the lowest since October 10, 2022, when it was 44.

The IMD warned of a new weather system brewing in the Bay of Bengal. A low-pressure area lying over the South Andaman Sea and adjoining regions is intensifying today.

"It is very likely to concentrate into a Depression over the southeast Bay of Bengal and adjoining areas of the Andaman & Nicobar Islands and the Andaman Sea around 31 October," the Met Dept said in its official release.

Following this development, the system is expected to move westward and then northward toward the Andhra Pradesh coast over the next two days.

Meanwhile, yesterday's well-marked low-pressure area-the remnant of Cyclone Arnab-has weakened and currently lies over north Chhattisgarh and adjoining East Madhya Pradesh.

Heavy Rain Alerts: Isolated heavy rainfall is expected in Arunachal Pradesh, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, and Kerala.

Severe Thunderstorms (40-50 kmph winds): Lightning and strong gusty winds are likely to hit Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and Karaikal.

Moderate Thunderstorms (30-40 kmph winds): Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Interior Karnataka are expected to experience lightning and gusty winds, with strong surface winds, particularly in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

General Thunderstorms: Isolated lightning and thunderstorms are expected across Coastal Karnataka and Chhattisgarh.

West Bengal shifted 12,000 people living along the Sankosh in Alipurduar district to safety, while Assam closely monitored the situation in vulnerable areas of Dhubri and Kokrajhar districts after the river's water level rose following a glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) in adjoining Bhutan, officials said.

Water level in the Sankosh, which forms the inter-state boundary between Assam and West Bengal, rose by nearly two feet since this morning after a glacial lake in Bhutan's Gasa region burst its banks on Thursday evening.

The incident triggered flood alerts in parts of north Bengal and Assam, with authorities keeping a close watch on the water levels of rivers flowing down from the Himalayan kingdom.

data.title: Why are banks closed in Gujarat today, despite it being 5th Saturday? State-wise bank holiday 31 Oct; PM Modi in Gujarat
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- Banks in Gujarat are closed today, Saturday, 31 October, despite it being the fifth Saturday of the month. The closure is not related to the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) regular second- and fourth-Saturday bank holiday rule.

Instead, banks in the state are observing a special public holiday declared by the Gujarat government. The Gujarat government has included 31 October in its list of public holidays for banks in 2026. Here's why banks are closed in Gujarat today, whether branches in other states are operating, and what other bank holidays are scheduled in the state this year.

The Gujarat Government has issued a notification dated 27 November 2025, announcing the public holiday list for banks in the state for 2026.

The notification, numbered GS/22/2025/JSR/2025/509/GH, was issued under Section 25 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Ahmedabad.

The notification states, "The Government of Gujarat, in consultation with Reserve Bank of India, Ahmedabad is pleased to declare the following days to be public holidays for banks in Gujarat during the year 2026."

Under this list, 31 October has been declared a bank holiday on account of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birth anniversary.

Therefore, bank branches across Gujarat, including those of the State Bank of India (SBI), HDFC Bank, Punjab National Bank (PNB) and other public- and private-sector lenders, will remain closed today.

The fifth Saturday is ordinarily a working day for banks. Under the RBI's existing arrangement, banks observe holidays on the second and fourth Saturdays of every month. However, state-specific holidays can also lead to bank closures on other days.

Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was born on 31 October 1875 in Nadiad, Gujarat. Popularly known as the 'Iron Man of India', he was a prominent freedom fighter and India's first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister.

His birth anniversary is observed as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day) to commemorate his contribution to national integration and unity. The Statue of Unity, the world's tallest statue, inaugurated in Gujarat in 2018, also honours his legacy.

According to the PM India website, Prime Minister Narendra Modi is on a two-day visit to Gujarat on 30 and 31 October. "On 31 October, at around 9 AM, Prime Minister will offer floral tributes at the Statue of Unity. Thereafter, at around 9:15 AM, he will lay the foundation stone, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects worth over Rs.400 crore in Ekta Nagar."

"Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday paid tributes to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel on his birth anniversary, saying he dedicated his life to the creation of a strong, prosperous, and capable India," according to a DD News report today.

At around 5:30 PM, the Prime Minister will participate in the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations commemorating the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

According to the Gujarat government's 2026 bank holiday notification, the following are the remaining holidays after 31 October:

No. October 31 is not a nationwide bank holiday. The closure applies to Gujarat under the state government's bank holiday notification. Therefore, bank branches in other states, including Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai, and others, will operate as usual.

data.title: Indian Railways to replace LPG, diesel with PNG at 22 sites under pact with IGL
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- Northern Railway will replace around 500 kg of LPG and 2,500 litres of diesel consumed daily across 22 railway establishments with piped natural gas (PNG), following a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed with Indraprastha Gas Limited (IGL).

The initial PNG consumption under the agreement is estimated at 3,000 Standard Cubic Metres per Day (SCMD), with demand expected to increase to 8,000-10,000 SCMD in the coming years as infrastructure and connectivity expand, IGL said in a statement on Saturday.

The agreement covers railway establishments across Delhi, Ghaziabad and Gautam Budh Nagar and is aimed at accelerating the adoption of natural gas among institutional and commercial consumers under the government's National PNG Drive 3.0.

Under the first phase, PNG will be supplied to 22 designated locations, including departmental mechanised laundries at Delhi Sarai Rohilla, Old Delhi, Anand Vihar Terminal, Hazrat Nizamuddin and New Delhi, where the fuel will be used for boiler operations.

The agreement also covers officers' rest houses, base kitchens, running rooms, subordinate rest houses and guard and Travelling Ticket Examiner (TTE) lobbies.

The partnership is expected to expand with the development of PNG infrastructure across IGL's authorised geographical areas, including Ajmer, Banda, Rewari and Muzaffarnagar.

Speaking on the occasion, Pushpesh Raman Tripathi, Divisional Railway Manager, Delhi Division, Northern Railway, said the agreement would help Indian Railways reduce substantial energy costs. He added that the railway administration plans to extend PNG connectivity to railway hospitals and residential colonies in the future.

Subhankar Sen, Chairman of IGL, said the collaboration would facilitate the substitution of a substantial quantity of LPG with natural gas, helping reduce import dependence and the associated subsidy burden.

He added that the initiative could pave the way for a wider transition from LPG to PNG across the Indian Railways network.

Kumar Shanker, Managing Director of IGL, described the partnership as a pioneering model of collaboration between Indian Railways and city gas distribution companies.

The MoU was signed in the presence of senior officials from both organisations, including Mohit Bhatia, Director (Commercial), IGL.

The initiative is expected to simplify fuel handling, improve supply reliability and support the transition towards cleaner energy sources across railway establishments.
